EV charging programs: what's still open

None of the dated EV charging solicitations we track is still open as of Nov 23, 2026. All three closed between Oct 9 and Nov 10. The one live lead is an installer partnership with Applegreen for its Maine NEVI sites, which has no deadline (CET opportunity radar).

What remains in play

  • Applegreen in Maine. The radar recommends offering Applegreen the same installer partnership pitched in Massachusetts. Together they could form a multi-state DC fast-charger pipeline.

Limits of this view

  • The radar was generated on Sep 24, 2026. It is about two months old and may miss newer postings.

Why EV depot work counts

The growth plan treats EV depot charging as one of the Phase 3 lines that turn one-off bids into recurring contracts. That service mix is the one PKF and Capstone price 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors. The plan targets roughly 25% recurring service by month 36 (est., labelled an assumption) (CET growth plan).

Winning installer status with NEVI developers now gives CET charger operations and maintenance revenue later, which is the part of the business that moves the multiple.

Next actions

  1. Rerun the radar for EV charging across all six states, including a manual pull of COMMBUYS, RI and NH portals.
  2. Contact Applegreen this month about its Maine NEVI installs. Use any MassDOT installer-call response as the reference.
  3. Confirm in the bid log whether CET responded to SRTA, Cambridge and the MassDOT call. Then chase award status and debriefs.
  4. Ask SRTA and other regional transit authorities about upcoming depot-charging phases, working from the Taunton office.

# EV charging programs: what's still open

**None of the dated EV charging solicitations we track is still open as of Nov 23, 2026.** All three closed between Oct 9 and Nov 10. The one live lead is an installer partnership with Applegreen for its Maine NEVI sites, which has no deadline (CET opportunity radar).

## Status as of today

| Program | Owner | Deadline | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| New Bedford DC fast-charger install | SRTA | Oct 9, 2026 | Closed |
| NEVI developers' installer call | MassDOT developers (Global Montello / Applegreen memo) | Oct 31, 2026 | Closed |
| Cambridge neighborhood EV charging (federal-aid) | City of Cambridge | Nov 10, 2026 | Closed |
| Maine NEVI installer partnership | Applegreen (2026 Maine NEVI awards) | None listed | Open lead, not a formal bid |

(CET opportunity radar)

## What remains in play

- **Applegreen in Maine.** The radar recommends offering Applegreen the same installer partnership pitched in Massachusetts. Together they could form a multi-state DC fast-charger pipeline.
- **Follow-through on closed items.** If CET responded to the MassDOT installer call or bid SRTA or Cambridge, awards and developer shortlists may still be pending. The context does not record whether CET submitted, so check internal bid logs.

## Limits of this view

- The radar was generated on Sep 24, 2026. It is about two months old and may miss newer postings.
- COMMBUYS, RI Purchasing and NH DAS blocked automated access. Massachusetts, Rhode Island and New Hampshire municipal EV bids may be under-counted (CET opportunity radar).
- No contract values are listed for any EV item. Sizing the pipeline would require award amounts from MassDOT, Maine DOT and the developers.

## Why EV depot work counts

The growth plan treats EV depot charging as one of the Phase 3 lines that turn one-off bids into recurring contracts. That service mix is the one PKF and Capstone price 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors. The plan targets roughly 25% recurring service by month 36 (est., labelled an assumption) (CET growth plan).

Winning installer status with NEVI developers now gives CET charger operations and maintenance revenue later, which is the part of the business that moves the multiple.

## Next actions

1. Rerun the radar for EV charging across all six states, including a manual pull of COMMBUYS, RI and NH portals.
2. Contact Applegreen this month about its Maine NEVI installs. Use any MassDOT installer-call response as the reference.
3. Confirm in the bid log whether CET responded to SRTA, Cambridge and the MassDOT call. Then chase award status and debriefs.
4. Ask SRTA and other regional transit authorities about upcoming depot-charging phases, working from the Taunton office.
